If you play Island now, you'll need to play Swiftwater Cliffs on turn 3 (entering tapped), delaying Commander's Sphere to turn 4. Playing Swiftwater Cliffs now and Island on turn 3 gives you Mountain + Swiftwater Cliffs + Island = 3 mana on turn 3 for Commander's Sphere.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Island
annotations.betterLine: Play Swiftwater Cliffs to get the tapped land out of the way early, enabling a turn 3 Commander's Sphere with Island played untapped on turn 3.

annotations.description: Playing a basic Mountain instead of Boros Garrison on turn 2 is suboptimal. Playing it on turn 2 (bouncing the existing Mountain) would mean having access to RW on turn 3 plus whatever other land is played. With expensive cards in hand like Combustible Gearhulk (6 mana) and Chain Reaction (4 mana), ramping via Boros Garrison early is important. Playing a basic Mountain instead delays the ramp by a turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played a basic Mountain as the turn 2 land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Boros Garrison, bouncing the existing Mountain back to hand. This provides RW mana starting turn 3 and effectively ramps toward the expensive spells in hand.

annotations.description: On turn 2 with a hand full of expensive spells (Call the Skybreaker at 7 mana, Elemental Masterpiece at 7, Treasure Cruise at 8, Fiery Encore at 5), the player chose a basic Mountain over Memorial to Genius or Blighted Cataract. While Memorial to Genius enters tapped (costing tempo this turn), it provides a built-in card draw engine later in the game. Blighted Cataract also enters tapped but offers similar utility. Given that the hand is extremely top-heavy with no plays before turn 3 at the earliest (Rootha at 3 mana), playing a tapped land on turn 2 costs very little tempo since there's nothing to cast anyway. Memorial to Genius would provide blue mana (useful for the U-heavy spells) plus a valuable card draw sacrifice ability for the mid-to-late game.
annotations.actionTaken: Played a basic Mountain as their land drop for turn 2.
annotations.betterLine: Play Memorial to Genius (or Blighted Cataract) since there are no 2-mana plays available anyway, and the tapped land would provide card draw utility later while still producing colored mana.

annotations.description: Temple of the False God only produces mana if you control five or more lands. With only 2 lands in play (Mountain, Island), Temple will be a dead land for several turns. Swiftwater Cliffs enters tapped but immediately provides colored mana (U or R) on the next turn, which helps cast Commander's Sphere on turn 4 or Pramikon on curve. Playing Temple now means having 3 lands but only 2 that can produce mana, effectively wasting the land drop's tempo.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Temple of the False God as the turn 3 land drop with only 2 other lands in play.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swiftwater Cliffs instead. It enters tapped but gains 1 life and provides colored mana next turn, enabling a turn 4 Commander's Sphere or setting up Pramikon. Save Temple of the False God for when closer to 5 lands.

annotations.description: With 8 cards in hand and only 7 allowed, Kimi25 will be forced to discard at end of turn. Alternatively, they could have discarded Elemental Masterpiece for {U/R}{U/R} to create a Treasure token, turning a dead discard into mana ramp.

annotations.betterLine: Use Fiery Fall's basic landcycling for {1}{R} to search for a basic land (likely an Island or Mountain), improving mana development while naturally reducing hand size. Alternatively, discard Elemental Masterpiece for {U/R}{U/R} to create a Treasure token.

annotations.description: Discarding Blighted Cataract (a land) instead of a high-cost spell is suboptimal. Kimi25 has only 2 lands on the battlefield and is behind on mana development. Blighted Cataract is a land that could be played next turn to help catch up, and it also has a useful late-game sacrifice ability for card draw. Meanwhile, cards like Call the Skybreaker (7 mana) or Elemental Masterpiece (7 mana) are extremely expensive and won't be castable for many turns. Elemental Masterpiece can even be discarded later for value (its channel ability creates a Treasure token), and Call the Skybreaker has retrace so it's actually better in the graveyard. Discarding a playable land when mana-screwed at 2 lands is a meaningful error.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Blighted Cataract, a land, while having only 2 lands on the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Call the Skybreaker, which costs 7 mana (uncastable for many turns) and has retrace (can be cast from graveyard later by discarding a land), making it essentially free to discard. Alternatively, discard Fiery Encore which is also expensive and situational. Keep Blighted Cataract to play as a land drop next turn.

Playing the tapped land delays mana development by a turn.

This accelerates to 5 permanents counting as lands/mana sources faster, enabling Temple of the False God and earlier casting of Pramikon or Crackling Drake. Swiftwater Cliffs could be played on a future turn when there's less pressure to use all mana.

More importantly, Fiery Fall has Basic Landcycling for {1}{R}, which means it can find any basic land and effectively acts as a land itself while also being a reasonable removal spell. Discarding it removes that flexibility. Meanwhile, several cards in hand like Call the Skybreaker and Elemental Masterpiece have retrace/discard synergies that specifically want land cards to discard - Desert of the Fervent would be perfect fuel for Call the Skybreaker's retrace or Elemental Masterpiece's treasure-making ability later. Keeping Fiery Fall (which finds lands) and Desert of the Fervent (which is discard fuel for retrace) would have been better than discarding the flexible Fiery Fall.

annotations.betterLine: Discard Desert of the Fervent or Fiery Encore. Desert is a low-impact tapped land when you have Memorial to Genius as a better land to play, and Fiery Encore requires setup that may not come together. Fiery Fall's landcycling is valuable when you're mana-light with only 2 lands in play.

In a 4-player game on turn 5 with no board presence and no blockers, Propaganda provides critical defensive value against attacks from multiple opponents. Baleful Strix is a fine blocker with deathtouch but only blocks one creature, while Propaganda taxes all attackers. The Strix's card draw is nice but Propaganda's persistent protection is more impactful at this stage. That said, Baleful Strix does draw a card and provide a deathtouch blocker, so this is debatable.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Propaganda for 2U to establish a tax on all attacking creatures, providing broader protection in a multiplayer game where multiple opponents could attack.

Playing Baleful Strix would have been better — it replaces itself and provides board presence, while Dungeon Map is a tempo-negative play that doesn't impact the board.

With only 4 lands (and Boros Garrison in hand which would bounce one), the 6-mana Combustible Gearhulk is expensive but represents a powerful threat with first strike and card draw/damage. More importantly, discarding Combustible Gearhulk to the graveyard has strong synergy with Feldon of the Third Path (which is still in hand) - Feldon can reanimate a copy of Gearhulk for just 2R, getting its ETB trigger. Chain Reaction is a board wipe that currently has limited value since there are very few creatures on the battlefield. However, Boros Garrison is a tap-land that bounces a land and doesn't accelerate much in a deck that needs to get to 6 mana for Sun Titan. Discarding Boros Garrison instead of Combustible Gearhulk would have been better - the Gearhulk is a premium Feldon target and a strong card to cast naturally, while Boros Garrison is a mediocre land. Actually, keeping Combustible Gearhulk as a Feldon target makes the Gearhulk discard somewhat defensible since it goes to the graveyard where Feldon wants it. But discarding both Chain Reaction AND Combustible Gearhulk means losing a board wipe. The better line was to discard Boros Garrison (a tapped land that bounces another land, poor tempo) and either Chain Reaction or Battlemage's Bracers. Actually, re-reading: Combustible Gearhulk in the graveyard IS good with Feldon. And Chain Reaction has limited current utility. But Boros Garrison should have been a discard candidate over Chain Reaction since Chain Reaction is a board wipe that could be critical later, and Reconstruct History can get it back. The discard of Chain Reaction over Boros Garrison is the questionable part.

annotations.betterLine: Discard Boros Garrison (mediocre tapped bounce-land) and Combustible Gearhulk (which becomes a Feldon target in the graveyard). This preserves Chain Reaction as a board wipe option and still sets up the Feldon + Gearhulk synergy.

However, looking at the choices, 'Unknown (bdae9dce)' is likely Rootha's bounce ability or a land play option. More importantly, Treasure Cruise could be cast here using Delve - with 3 cards in the graveyard (Blighted Cataract, Fiery Fall, Desert of the Fervent), they could exile all 3 to cast Treasure Cruise for just 4U (5 mana total), which they have available (Island, Mountain, Memorial to Genius, Desert of the Mindful, Mountain = 5 lands plus Rootha). Drawing 3 cards for 5 mana is far better than holding up a 5-mana counterspell, especially when the hand is full of expensive spells and needs to develop. The player has 6 lands (including Rootha which isn't a land) - actually 5 lands. With 5 mana they could Delve away 3 cards and pay 4U for Treasure Cruise, drawing 3 fresh cards to find lands and cheaper interaction. Instead casting Traumatic Visions as a counterspell means tapping out anyway but getting no card advantage, and holding a clunky 5-mana counter is poor when you need to develop your board. Actually, re-reading - they may be casting it for its basic landcycling ({1}{U}) to search for a basic land, which would cost only 2 mana and fix/ramp. That's more reasonable but still worse than Treasure Cruise which draws 3 cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast/cycled Traumatic Visions instead of casting Treasure Cruise with Delve
annotations.betterLine: Cast Treasure Cruise delving away the 3 graveyard cards (Blighted Cataract, Fiery Fall, Desert of the Fervent) to draw 3 cards for 4U, getting much more card advantage and finding lands/action

Additionally, Gramps has Phantom Steed in hand which could exile and repeatedly copy the Strix for value if it stays on the battlefield. Trading away the Strix for 1 damage is low value compared to keeping it as a blocker and Phantom Steed target.

If Gramps plans to cast Sunblast Angel in a future turn (or even this turn in main phase 2), having their own Baleful Strix tapped would mean it gets destroyed by their own Sunblast Angel. Additionally, Baleful Strix is a 1/1 with deathtouch and flying - attacking into a board where Kimi25 Libby has Talrand (2/2) and Rootha available, and the attack direction matters in a Pramikon game. The Strix is more valuable as a blocker with deathtouch and Propaganda is already discouraging attacks. However, the 1 damage chip is very marginal and risks losing a deathtouch blocker that synergizes with Propaganda for defense. The real cost is minor since the Strix has already drawn its card, but attacking it into potential blocks or tapping it before a potential Sunblast Angel play is slightly suboptimal.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Baleful Strix (1/1 flying deathtouch)
annotations.betterLine: Hold Baleful Strix back as a deathtouch blocker to complement Propaganda's defensive strategy, especially with Sunblast Angel in hand that would destroy your own tapped creatures.

The mana was going unused anyway.

annotations.betterLine: Discard Elemental Masterpiece using its {U/R}{U/R} ability to create a Treasure token, gaining ramp toward expensive spells like Call the Skybreaker or Inferno Project while growing Inferno Project's counter count.

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley has 8 lands (including Temple of the False God for 2 mana and Commander's Sphere for 1) giving access to approximately 9 mana. Playing Guttersnipe (3 mana) is fine value, but Pramikon, Sky Rampart (3 mana URW) is a strong defensive option that controls combat in a 4-player game, and River Kelpie (5 mana) provides card draw whenever permanents enter from graveyards (synergizing with graveyard strategies). However, the bigger consideration is sequencing: playing Empowered Autogenerator (4 mana) this turn would start accumulating charge counters for future mana acceleration, which is important given Zetalpa (8 mana) sitting in hand. Playing Guttersnipe is only good if you plan to chain instants/sorceries, but with Increasing Vengeance and Oona's Grace in the graveyard and few instant/sorcery spells in hand, the immediate payoff is limited. Empowered Autogenerator + Guttersnipe could both be cast this turn (4+3 = 7 mana, and they have ~9 available), making the sequencing of which to cast first relevant but both castable. The real question is whether Guttersnipe alone is the best single play versus deploying Empowered Autogenerator first to start ramping toward Zetalpa.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Guttersnipe (3 mana) as the first spell in postcombat main.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Empowered Autogenerator first (to start charge counter accumulation toward casting Zetalpa), then cast Guttersnipe with remaining mana. Both could likely be cast this turn with ~9 mana available.

annotations.description: Only attacking with Rootha (1/4) instead of both creatures when there are opponents with no blockers available. MiMo Timmy has no creatures and Llama4 Valley is fully tapped. Talrand as a 2/2 isn't a meaningful blocker, and there's free damage being left on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Rootha, Mercurial Artist (1 power) while keeping Talrand, Sky Summoner back.

MiMo Timmy at 40hp has only 4 lands and no creatures on board - attacking MiMo would avoid the Propaganda tax entirely and apply pressure to a vulnerable opponent with a weak board state. Additionally, GPT5m Gramps has Baleful Strix (a 1/1 deathtouch flyer) that could block one attacker favorably.

annotations.betterLine: Attack MiMo Timmy instead to avoid paying the Propaganda tax and pressure the opponent with the weakest board position.

While the damage is small (1-3 points), there's essentially no downside to attacking an undefended player — Rootha is a 1/4 that survives most combat and Talrand is a 2/2 that could chip in. The reasoning given ('lending fees remain usurious') references Propaganda but that only applies to attacking Gramps. Free damage should generally be taken in Commander, especially when it costs nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack MiMo Timmy (who has no blockers and no board presence) with Talrand, Sky Summoner and/or Rootha, Mercurial Artist for 2-3 free damage. Rootha could be kept back if you want the option to bounce it for spell copying, but Talrand has no reason not to swing.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps attacked with Baleful Strix (1/1 flying deathtouch) into a board where Kimi25 Libby has Rootha, Mercurial Artist and Talrand, Sky Summoner. Baleful Strix is a valuable defensive piece - its deathtouch makes it an excellent blocker that deters attacks, and it synergizes with Phantom Steed in hand (exile it, get repeated ETB draws). With Propaganda already providing attack deterrence, the Strix is more valuable as a blocker/combo piece than as a 1-damage attacker. However, the 1 flying damage is free if nobody blocks, and Pramikon isn't on the battlefield to restrict attack directions, so the risk depends on who can block. Kimi25 Libby doesn't appear to have flying blockers currently, so the Strix would likely get through for 1. The risk is minimal but the upside is also minimal - 1 damage in a 4-player game at 37+ life totals is nearly irrelevant, while losing the Strix to any flash creature or combat trick would be bad.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Baleful Strix
annotations.betterLine: Hold back Baleful Strix as a deathtouch blocker and potential Phantom Steed target for card advantage. The 1 flying damage is negligible in multiplayer, and the Strix provides much more value on defense and as a combo piece with Phantom Steed.

annotations.description: During combat (on their own turn), Llama4 Valley chose to sacrifice Commander's Sphere to draw a card. Commander's Sphere is a mana rock that provides colored mana, and sacrificing it permanently removes a mana source. With expensive cards in hand like Zetalpa (8 mana) and only 8 lands/mana sources, losing a mana rock is significant. Additionally, this is their own combat step - they could use Oona's Grace (an instant) to draw a card by discarding a land, which is generally available from the graveyard via retrace anyway. More importantly, they could simply pass here and use Commander's Sphere for mana on future turns to cast their expensive spells, or at minimum wait until end of an opponent's turn to sacrifice it if they really want the card draw.
annotations.actionTaken: Sacrificed Commander's Sphere to draw a card during their own combat step
annotations.betterLine: Pass without activating either ability, preserving Commander's Sphere as a mana source to help cast expensive cards like Zetalpa, Primal Dawn (8 mana) and Pramikon, Sky Rampart. If card draw was needed, use Oona's Grace from graveyard instead, or at minimum wait until an opponent's end step to sacrifice the Sphere.

The reasoning suggests they thought this would 'disrupt' the opponent, but drawing a card is always beneficial for the recipient. Llama4 Valley essentially spent a land and mana to help an opponent while getting nothing themselves.

annotations.betterLine: Target themselves with Oona's Grace to draw a card, since the whole point of retracing Oona's Grace is card filtering/advantage for yourself.

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley cast Increasing Vengeance via Flashback (costing {3}{R}{R}) to copy Oona's Grace, which is an opponent's spell (Kimi25 Libby likely cast it). Increasing Vengeance can only target an instant or sorcery spell *you control*. Since Oona's Grace is not Llama4's spell, this is an illegal target, wasting the Flashback cast and exiling Increasing Vengeance for nothing. Even if the targeting were somehow valid, spending 5 mana and exiling a powerful spell from the graveyard just to copy a 'draw one card' spell is extremely poor value. The Commander's Sphere sacrifice (draw a card) or simply passing would have been far better uses of resources.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Increasing Vengeance from graveyard via Flashback targeting Oona's Grace (an opponent's spell), paying {3}{R}{R} and exiling Increasing Vengeance.
annotations.betterLine: Either sacrifice Commander's Sphere to draw a card, or simply pass without spending resources. Increasing Vengeance should be saved for copying one of your own high-value spells, not wasted on an opponent's cantrip (which is an illegal target anyway).

annotations.description: MiMo Timmy cast Battlemage's Bracers (2R) before considering whether to use Feldon's ability this turn. With 5 lands (4 Mountains + 1 Plains + 1 Secluded Steppe), casting Bracers costs 3 mana, leaving only 2 mana available. Feldon's ability costs 2R+tap, so Timmy can't both cast Bracers AND activate Feldon this turn. Furthermore, equipping Bracers costs another 2 mana, so even next turn it would require 5 mana just to equip and activate Feldon. Hedron Archive (4 generic) would have been a strong alternative - it provides ramp to enable Feldon activations on future turns more reliably, and can be sacrificed for card draw later. Alternatively, casting Thopter Engineer (2R) would create an artifact creature token and give artifact creatures haste, providing board presence. The Bracers are only valuable once equipped to Feldon and activated, which requires significant additional mana investment. However, Bracers + Feldon is a powerful combo that doubles his reanimation value, so planning ahead for it is defensible.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Battlemage's Bracers for 2R, leaving only 2 mana and unable to activate Feldon this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Hedron Archive (4 mana) for ramp, enabling Feldon activation next turn with more mana available, or cast Thopter Engineer for immediate board presence and haste for artifact creatures.

Combustible Gearhulk would also be a strong choice as a 6/6 first striker with card draw/damage ETB. The reasoning in the decision even acknowledges Triplicate Titan is huge but then pivots away without good justification.

annotations.description: Call the Skybreaker has Retrace, meaning it can be cast from the graveyard by discarding a land card. Discarding it to hand size actually makes it MORE accessible since it can be reused from the graveyard. However, Sol Ring costs only {1} and produces 2 mana - it's one of the most powerful cards in Commander and should have been played long ago (it only costs 1 mana). The real issue is that Sol Ring is still in hand on turn 15, and rather than discarding a less impactful card, the player chose Call the Skybreaker. While Call the Skybreaker with Retrace is fine to discard, the bigger problem is that Sol Ring should have been cast this turn or earlier. Looking at the board, Kimi25 Libby has 6 lands and Rootha + Talrand untapped - they had mana available to cast Sol Ring ({1}) at some point. Additionally, discarding Elemental Masterpiece would have been better since it has a discard ability that creates a Treasure token ({U/R}{U/R}, discard: create Treasure), but that requires paying mana. Actually, Call the Skybreaker with Retrace from graveyard is arguably better positioned there than in hand, so this discard isn't terrible. The real blunder is having Sol Ring in hand on turn 15 - but since the decision point is specifically about the discard, and Call the Skybreaker is actually a reasonable discard due to Retrace, the main issue is not discarding something less useful. Traumatic Visions or Talisman of Creativity could have been discarded instead, but Sol Ring at 1 mana should have been cast, and keeping it in hand to cast next turn is correct. Call the Skybreaker with Retrace from graveyard is actually a fine discard choice.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Call the Skybreaker while still holding Sol Ring on turn 15
annotations.betterLine: Sol Ring should have been cast earlier in the turn (it costs only {1}), then discard would be from 7 cards. Call the Skybreaker is actually a reasonable retrace discard, but having Sol Ring uncast on turn 15 represents significant lost tempo across the game.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps is attacking with Baleful Strix (1/1 flying deathtouch) into a board where they have Propaganda protecting them. The Strix is a valuable defensive piece - it has deathtouch and flying, making it an excellent blocker that deters attacks. Attacking with it exposes it to potential blocks or removal, and the 1 damage is fairly insignificant in a 4-player game where opponents are at 28-39 life. Additionally, the attack direction matters - they need to attack someone specific, and 1 damage is negligible. However, Baleful Strix has already drawn its card, and with flying it's unlikely to be blocked profitably. The deathtouch flying body is still useful as a deterrent blocker though, and losing it to a combat trick or unexpected block would be unfortunate. This is debatable - the 1 chip damage has some value, but keeping the deathtouch blocker back is also reasonable, especially when GPT5m Gramps is at 28 life and relying on Propaganda for defense.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Baleful Strix
annotations.betterLine: Hold back Baleful Strix as a deathtouch flying blocker to complement Propaganda's defensive strategy, especially since 1 damage is negligible and the defensive value of deathtouch is significant

annotations.description: Prismatic Strands is a defensive combat trick that prevents all damage from sources of a chosen color for the turn. Casting it during your own precombat main phase, when no opponent is attacking you and there's no damage to prevent, accomplishes absolutely nothing. The card is wasted for zero value. It has flashback (tap an untapped white creature you control), but the initial cast from hand is completely thrown away here. Deep Analysis from the graveyard (flashback for {1}{U} and 3 life) would have drawn 2 cards, and River Kelpie would have triggered (drawing another card when casting from graveyard), giving massive card advantage. Rolling Temblor from graveyard (flashback {4}{R}{R}) could also have been cast with River Kelpie synergy. Even Ral Zarek would have been a reasonable play adding a planeswalker to the board.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Prismatic Strands from hand during own precombat main phase with no damage to prevent, wasting the card entirely.

annotations.description: MiMo Timmy has 6 lands (4 Mountains, 1 Plains, 1 Secluded Steppe) plus Feldon of the Third Path on the battlefield. With Feldon, they can already create token copies of creatures in the graveyard (like Triplicate Titan, Combustible Gearhulk, or Meteor Golem). The key issue is that Mind Stone is a 2-mana rock when they already have 6 lands and could instead be casting Sun Titan (4WW = 6 mana). Sun Titan is a 6/6 vigilance that returns permanents with MV 3 or less from graveyard to battlefield - it could bring back Thousand-Year Elixir (which synergizes amazingly with Feldon by letting him activate twice), Boros Garrison (ramp), or other key pieces. MiMo's mana is 4 Mountains + 1 Plains + 1 Secluded Steppe = they can produce 4R + 1W + 1W = 4RWW. Sun Titan costs 4WW, which is exactly castable with this mana. Playing Mind Stone instead means Sun Titan gets delayed a turn while providing minimal benefit since they already have enough mana for their key plays.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mind Stone for 2 mana, a ramp artifact that provides minimal benefit at 6 lands
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sun Titan (4WW) using all 6 lands. Sun Titan enters and triggers, returning Thousand-Year Elixir from graveyard to battlefield, enabling double Feldon activations in future turns. This is a much higher-impact play.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Libby has Rootha (1/4) and Talrand (2/2) on the board. GPT5m Gramps has Propaganda up requiring {2} per attacker, making attacking there expensive. With no blockers that threaten to kill either creature favorably, attacking with at least Rootha (1 power, 4 toughness - very hard to lose in combat) into an opponent without Propaganda would be free chip damage. Declining to attack when you have safe attacks available leaves damage on the table.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Libby played a Mountain from hand instead of casting Sol Ring, which costs only 1 mana and would provide 2 colorless mana immediately. Sol Ring is one of the most efficient mana accelerants in Commander and should almost always be cast as early as possible. With 6 lands already on the battlefield (plus the Mountain about to be played making 7), they have plenty of colored sources. Playing the land is fine, but Sol Ring should have been cast as well - they had the mana to do both. Looking at the choices, Sol Ring costs {1} and they have untapped lands available. They could play Mountain AND cast Sol Ring, plus potentially cast Talisman of Creativity or even Treasure Cruise (with delve fuel from 8 cards in graveyard). By just playing Mountain and passing, they wasted significant mana and tempo.

annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain, then cast Sol Ring (1 mana), then cast Talisman of Creativity (2 mana from Sol Ring), and potentially cast Treasure Cruise using delve with remaining mana. At minimum, Sol Ring should have been cast this turn.

More importantly, the attack is into a board where the damage is minimal (1 damage) and Baleful Strix is much more valuable as a blocker with deathtouch, especially with Propaganda already providing defensive coverage. The risk of losing the Strix to blocks or removing it as a blocker far outweighs 1 point of damage. Additionally, with Sunblast Angel in hand, keeping creatures untapped is strategically important for when that angel is cast - you want opponents' creatures tapped, not your own.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Libby cast Dualcaster Mage targeting Elemental Masterpiece on the stack. However, Elemental Masterpiece is a sorcery that creates two 4/4 Elemental tokens - copying it would give Kimi two additional 4/4 tokens, which is strong. But the issue is that the Elemental Masterpiece on the stack appears to be the discard ability of the card ('{U/R}{U/R}, Discard this card: Create a Treasure token'), not the sorcery itself being cast. Looking at the graveyard, Elemental Masterpiece is already in Kimi's graveyard, meaning it was discarded to create a Treasure token. Dualcaster Mage copies an instant or sorcery spell, but the Treasure-creating ability is an activated ability, not a spell. This means the Dualcaster Mage's ETB trigger would have no valid target and accomplish nothing beyond getting a 2/2 body. The Dualcaster Mage was wasted as a copy effect when it could have been held for a more impactful spell to copy later.

annotations.betterLine: Hold Dualcaster Mage for a future high-value instant or sorcery spell to copy, such as an opponent's removal spell or a powerful draw spell. At 6 life, saving resources for defensive plays would be more prudent.

With only 5 mana sources total and expensive cards like Sunblast Angel (6 mana) and Arcane Endeavor (7 mana) in hand, they are severely mana-starved and should prioritize playing a land first. Lightning Greaves with no creatures on the battlefield accomplishes very little right now - there's nothing to equip it to. Playing Thriving Moor or Arcane Sanctum would help work toward casting their powerful spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lightning Greaves before playing a land, with no creatures on the battlefield to equip.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Moor or Arcane Sanctum first to develop mana, then consider casting Lightning Greaves if mana permits. With only 2 lands and no creatures, the land drop is far more important.

annotations.description: Discarded Utter End, a flexible 4-mana instant exile spell, when Arcane Endeavor (7 mana) is essentially uncastable given GPT5m Gramps has only 2 lands on the battlefield and desperately needs to develop mana before casting expensive spells. Utter End would be castable much sooner and provides critical removal against Llama4 Valley's threats in what is now a 1v1 situation while behind on board and life.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Utter End
annotations.betterLine: Discard Arcane Endeavor, which costs 7 mana and is far too expensive to realistically cast given the severely mana-starved board state (only 2 lands + 3 mana rocks). Keep Utter End as efficient removal for the 1v1 against Llama4 Valley.

annotations.description: At end of turn with 8 mana available (7 lands + Temple of the False God producing 2), Llama4 Valley declined to use Oona's Grace (2U instant) to draw a card by discarding one of the three Islands in hand. With 3 excess Islands in hand and needing to find impactful spells, converting a land into a draw at instant speed on the opponent's end step is pure upside. Additionally, Armillary Sphere could have been activated to fetch basic lands, thinning the deck, though that requires sacrificing it. Oona's Grace is the clearest missed opportunity - it's a mana sink that converts dead cards into live draws.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without using any instant-speed abilities despite having open mana and cards to use.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Oona's Grace from graveyard (via Retrace) by paying 2U and discarding one of the three Islands in hand to draw a card, making use of excess lands and open mana.

annotations.description: Arcane Endeavor is a powerful 7-mana spell that draws multiple cards and potentially lets you cast a free spell. With only 5 lands (Nimbus Maze, Swamp) and 2 mana rocks (Arcane Signet, Dungeon Map) on the battlefield, GPT5m Gramps is far from casting it immediately, but it's one of the most impactful cards in hand. Meanwhile, they have 3 lands in hand (Plains, Plains, Arcane Sanctum, Thriving Moor) which are redundant. In a 1v1 situation against Llama4 Valley who has River Kelpie generating value, Arcane Endeavor could be a game-swinging play once enough mana is available. Discarding a land like a duplicate Plains would be far better since they have multiple lands in hand already and need to play one per turn anyway.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Arcane Endeavor, a 7-mana draw spell that could draw many cards and cast a free spell.
annotations.betterLine: Discard a duplicate Plains instead, keeping Arcane Endeavor as a powerful late-game card. With Thriving Moor, Arcane Sanctum, and Plains still in hand, there are plenty of land drops available, and one Plains is expendable.

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley has Oona's Grace in graveyard with Retrace, River Kelpie on battlefield (which draws a card whenever a spell is cast from graveyard), 8 cards in hand (needs to discard to 7), and multiple excess lands in hand. Casting Oona's Grace via Retrace would draw 2 cards (one from Grace, one from River Kelpie trigger) at the cost of discarding a land they'd need to discard anyway, effectively turning a dead land into 2 new cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without doing anything, presumably discarding a land to hand size for no value.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Oona's Grace from graveyard via Retrace (discarding a spare land like Island), drawing 2 cards (Oona's Grace + River Kelpie trigger), then discard down to 7 with better card selection.

An extra Island has more utility for enabling expensive flashback costs (Sevinne's Reclamation flashback at 4W, Ignite the Future flashback at 7R) or future land drops.

annotations.betterLine: Discard Bloodthirsty Blade, which is nearly useless (or actively harmful) in a 1v1 matchup

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps has only 5 lands (Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Arcane Signet, Propaganda, Dungeon Map - actually only 2 lands plus artifacts). Looking at the board, they have Nimbus Maze and Swamp as lands, plus Arcane Signet, Propaganda, and Dungeon Map as non-land permanents. They have 3 land options in hand (Thriving Moor, Plains, Arcane Sanctum) and should play a land first before casting spells. Obsessive Stitcher costs 1UB, which they can likely pay, but by casting it before playing a land, they lose flexibility. More importantly, they should play a land drop first (it's free) and then decide what to cast. Playing Thriving Moor (untapped with a color choice) or Plains would give them more mana available for the turn. The sequencing of casting a creature before playing a land is suboptimal - you should always play your land first to maximize available mana, unless there's a specific reason not to.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Obsessive Stitcher before playing a land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (Thriving Moor choosing white, or Plains), then cast Obsessive Stitcher with more mana available, keeping options open for the turn.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps discarded Thriving Moor while severely mana-screwed with only 2 lands in play (Nimbus Maze and Swamp). They desperately need land drops to develop their board. annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Thriving Moor, a land that produces black plus a chosen color
annotations.betterLine: Discard Meteor Golem (7 mana, nearly uncastable given current mana state) or Sunblast Angel (6 mana) and keep the land to make crucial land drops to catch up on mana development.

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley discarded Command Tower, which is a land that enters untapped and produces any color in their commander's color identity. They currently have only 8 lands on the battlefield and a hand full of lands they need to deploy. Command Tower is strictly better than basic Plains or Island since it taps for any color. They also have Evolving Wilds which enters tapped and requires sacrificing, making it worse than Command Tower in most situations. Given that the player has color-intensive spells in their graveyard (like Sevinne's Reclamation, Deep Analysis) and needs color fixing, discarding a color-fixing land that enters untapped over a basic land or Evolving Wilds is a clear mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Command Tower
annotations.betterLine: Discard a basic Island or Plains instead, keeping Command Tower as the superior mana-fixing land to play on a future turn. They already have 3 Islands on the battlefield, so discarding an Island would be most reasonable.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps cast Lightning Greaves (2 mana) before playing a land. Playing Fellwar Stone or playing a land first would be better sequencing. More importantly, with only 5 mana sources and expensive cards in hand (Meteor Golem at 7, Sunblast Angel at 6), developing mana with Fellwar Stone seems more productive than deploying equipment with no creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lightning Greaves with no creatures on board to equip it to.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains first, then cast Fellwar Stone to accelerate toward casting Sunblast Angel or Meteor Golem. Lightning Greaves provides no value without creatures on board.

annotations.betterLine: Play Arcane Sanctum (or Plains) first to increase mana production, then consider discarding Radiant Solar afterward if still desired.

annotations.description: Runic Repetition returns an exiled card with flashback to hand. Llama4 Valley has multiple flashback cards in the graveyard (Sevinne's Reclamation, Ignite the Future, Deep Analysis, Prismatic Strands, Oona's Grace, Rolling Temblor) that could potentially be cast from the graveyard and then exiled, making Runic Repetition a useful recursion tool. Discarding a tapland like Highland Lake (which enters tapped and is slow) or a basic land (Island or Plains, since they already have multiple sources) would preserve more future options. Runic Repetition requires a card to already be in exile with flashback, so it's somewhat situational, but given the number of flashback cards in the graveyard, it has real potential value. Discarding a land when at 8 lands with several lands in hand would have been better.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Runic Repetition

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps discarded Sunblast Angel, a powerful 4/5 flyer that destroys all tapped creatures on ETB. With only 2 lands and some mana rocks on the battlefield (Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Arcane Signet, Dungeon Map), they're struggling to reach 6 mana for the Angel, but it's one of the strongest cards in hand as a board wipe effect. Meteor Golem costs 7 mana and is harder to cast, while Sunblast Angel at 6 mana is a more efficient removal spell that could swing the game. However, Eternal Dragon has plainscycling to help find lands, and Fellwar Stone helps ramp, so keeping those makes sense. The real question is whether Sunblast Angel or Meteor Golem should be discarded - Sunblast Angel is generally stronger since it's a one-sided wipe against aggressive opponents (destroying tapped creatures after combat), while Meteor Golem destroys any single nonland permanent. With Llama4 Valley being the only remaining opponent with River Kelpie on board, Sunblast Angel could be a game-changer if the Kelpie attacks and becomes tapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Sunblast Angel
annotations.betterLine: Discard Meteor Golem instead - it costs more mana (7 vs 6) and Sunblast Angel's board wipe effect against tapped creatures is more impactful in a 1v1 situation where the opponent needs to attack to win.

annotations.description: Discarding Eternal Dragon when it has plainscycling ({2} to search for a Plains) and can recur itself from the graveyard during upkeep for {3}{W}{W}. However, GPT5m Gramps only has 2 lands (Nimbus Maze and Swamp) plus Arcane Signet and Dungeon Map for mana, making it very mana-starved. Eternal Dragon's recursion ability could be valuable later, but the player may be planning to use Unburial Rites on better targets. The real concern is that discarding Eternal Dragon over a Plains means losing a card that can generate card advantage from the graveyard (plainscycling from hand is lost, but the upkeep recursion still works from graveyard). Actually, since Eternal Dragon can return itself from graveyard to hand during upkeep, discarding it is somewhat reasonable - it's not permanently lost. But discarding a Plains instead would preserve the option of plainscycling Eternal Dragon while in hand, which could help fix the severe mana issues (only 2 lands on battlefield). With Unburial Rites in hand and powerful creatures in graveyard, keeping the Dragon and discarding a Plains is debatable since the player needs lands desperately.

annotations.betterLine: Discard a Plains instead, keeping Eternal Dragon in hand for its plainscycling ability ({2} to search for a Plains to hand), which helps address the severe mana screw (only 2 lands on battlefield). Plainscycling would be more immediately useful than the slow upkeep recursion.

Meteor Golem costs 7 mana which is very hard to cast, but it's also a reanimation target. However, Sun Titan provides recurring value every attack. The key issue is that discarding Meteor Golem removes a decent reanimation target when the player should be discarding a Plains (they have two Plains in hand and limited colored mana sources - they need Arcane Sanctum for color fixing far more than a second Plains).

Keeping Meteor Golem preserves it as a reanimation target via Unburial Rites to destroy an opponent's nonland permanent, or it could be hardcast later. Alternatively, discard Sun Titan to set up reanimating it with Unburial Rites next turn for immediate value.

With Pramikon choosing left, Llama4 Valley may need to attack GPT5m Gramps, making Propaganda a significant obstacle. Arcane Signet is just minor mana fixing that GPT5m Gramps can likely replace, while Propaganda is a persistent defensive enchantment that directly hinders Llama4 Valley's ability to deal damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Arcane Signet with Ray of Distortion
annotations.betterLine: Target Propaganda with Ray of Distortion to remove the tax on attacking GPT5m Gramps

annotations.description: Magmaquake is on the stack which would kill River Kelpie and Guttersnipe (creatures without flying). Prismatic Strands was available as a flashback option and could prevent all damage from red sources, saving these key creatures. River Kelpie is an important card advantage engine and Guttersnipe deals damage to opponents whenever instants/sorceries are cast.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Prismatic Strands, allowing Magmaquake to resolve and kill their creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Prismatic Strands from graveyard via flashback, choosing red to prevent all damage from Magmaquake, preserving River Kelpie and Guttersnipe.

annotations.description: Port Town doesn't have the Plains or Island land type, so it doesn't unlock Nimbus Maze's colored mana abilities. Playing a basic Plains would have enabled Nimbus Maze to tap for {U}, providing better color coverage (W+U+B+C vs W-or-U+B+C+C). Port Town should be saved for later when it can enter untapped while preserving basics for Nimbus Maze synergy.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Port Town as their land for the turn
annotations.betterLine: Play a basic Plains to unlock Nimbus Maze's {U} ability, saving Port Town for a later turn

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps has only 6 lands in play (Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Port Town, Propaganda, Dungeon Map, Lightning Greaves - actually only 3 lands: Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Port Town) and needs to develop mana. Casting Curator of Mysteries costs {2}{U}{U} which requires 4 mana, but with only 3 lands (Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Port Town) plus Dungeon Map for colorless, that's only 4 mana sources with potentially only 1-2 blue. More importantly, they should play a land first before casting spells. They have Plains, Island, Swamp, and Arcane Sanctum in hand. Playing a land first (like Island for blue mana) would help ensure they can cast the Curator and still have options. The correct sequencing is always to play land before casting spells unless there's a specific reason not to.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Curator of Mysteries before playing a land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island (or another land) first, then cast Curator of Mysteries. This ensures you don't miss your land drop and maximizes available mana.

annotations.description: Discarding a Swamp instead of Unburial Rites when Unburial Rites has a flashback cost ({3}{W}) that is cheaper and easier to pay than its regular mana cost ({4}{B}). With only 1 Swamp on battlefield, casting Unburial Rites from hand for {4}{B} is difficult, while flashing it back for {3}{W} is easier given their white mana sources. The extra Swamp would also help with future land drops.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Swamp
annotations.betterLine: Discard Unburial Rites to use its cheaper flashback cost of {3}{W} from the graveyard, while keeping the Swamp for mana development

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley has Zetalpa, Primal Dawn (4/8 flying, double strike, vigilance, trample, indestructible), Pristine Skywise (6/4 flying), and Elsha of the Infinite on the battlefield. With Pramikon choosing left, they can attack the nearest opponent in that direction. Both Kimi25 Libby (-13hp) and MiMo Timmy (-3hp) are already eliminated, leaving GPT5m Gramps at 25hp as the only remaining opponent. Zetalpa alone deals 8 damage (double strike) and Pristine Skywise deals 6, for 14 damage. GPT5m Gramps has Propaganda requiring {2} per attacker, but Llama4 Valley has Temple of the False God and other lands to pay for attackers. Even paying for Propaganda, attacking with the flyers would deal significant damage. Instead, Llama4 Valley chose not to attack at all, leaving 14+ damage on the table against the last remaining opponent.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures, passing the combat phase entirely.
annotations.betterLine: Attack GPT5m Gramps with at least Zetalpa (8 damage with double strike, has vigilance so stays untapped) and Pristine Skywise (6 damage), paying Propaganda costs. This would deal 14 damage, bringing Gramps from 25 to 11 life, putting them in lethal range next turn.

annotations.description: Playing Mountain when they already have red mana sources (Mountain + Swiftwater Cliffs) and could benefit from other untapped lands like Exotic Orchard (which provides flexible color access based on opponents' lands) or Plains (for white mana to enable flashback spells like Sevinne's Reclamation or Prismatic Strands). The player has multiple graveyard spells requiring white mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain as land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Exotic Orchard for color flexibility, or Plains to improve white mana access for graveyard flashback spells like Sevinne's Reclamation ({2}{W}) and Prismatic Strands

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley has 7 cards in hand but only 8 lands on the battlefield (including Temple of the False God). They should play a land before passing - they have multiple land options (Boros Guildgate, Plains, Exotic Orchard, Mystic Monastery, Azorius Chancery) and missing a land drop wastes development. Additionally, with only Pramikon on board and a graveyard full of flashback/retrace spells, they could cast Deep Analysis (flashback {1}{U}, pay 3 life) to draw cards, or cast other spells. The Empowered Autogenerator from the prior context also seems to have disappeared from the battlefield, suggesting something happened. At minimum, playing a land is free value that should never be skipped.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing a land or casting any spells during precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land (e.g., Exotic Orchard for immediate untapped mana, or Mystic Monastery for color fixing), then consider casting Deep Analysis via flashback or other available spells before passing.

annotations.description: Cast Rod of Absorption before playing a land drop. With only 3 colored-mana lands on the battlefield and being severely mana-screwed (needing to reach 5-6 mana for Unburial Rites or Sun Titan), the land drop should come first. Additionally, Rod of Absorption is a questionable priority when the immediate need is to develop mana and get threats on board to compete with Llama4 Valley's 39 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Rod of Absorption for 3 mana before playing a land
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (Plains or Island to fix mana), then decide whether to cast Rod of Absorption or save mana for other plays. Getting to 5+ mana for Unburial Rites targeting Sun Titan or other powerful creatures should be the priority.

annotations.description: Playing Plains when Exotic Orchard was available in hand. Exotic Orchard enters untapped and can produce W (same as Plains) plus U and potentially B from opponents' lands, making it strictly better in this position. The extra color flexibility matters for casting spells like Leadership Vacuum (2U), Chemister's Insight (3U), and various flashback spells from the graveyard.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Plains as their land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Exotic Orchard instead of Plains, preserving Plains for a turn where no better land is available. Exotic Orchard provides the same white mana plus additional color options.

annotations.description: Playing Arcane Sanctum (enters tapped) instead of an untapped land when Rod of Absorption (2U) could be cast this turn. With only 3 lands in play and needing to develop the board in a 1v1 against an opponent at 39 life, the tempo loss of a tapped land is meaningful.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Arcane Sanctum, which enters tapped, leaving only 3 untapped mana sources and unable to cast Rod of Absorption this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island untapped, then cast Rod of Absorption (2U) using Island + Nimbus Maze + Port Town/Swamp to start building value and disrupting the opponent's spells.

annotations.description: In a 1v1 against Llama4 Valley at 39 life, GPT5m Gramps chose to cast Rod of Absorption ({2}{U}) instead of playing a land and deploying Sun Titan (6 mana), which would immediately return a permanent with MV 3 or less from their stacked graveyard (Baleful Strix, Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone, etc.) and present a 6/6 vigilance threat. Rod of Absorption is a slow setup card that does nothing immediately in a 1v1 endgame where board presence matters far more.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Rod of Absorption for {2}{U}
annotations.betterLine: Play a land (Island or Plains), then cast Sun Titan for {4}{W}{W}, triggering its ETB to return a key permanent like Baleful Strix or Arcane Signet from graveyard, establishing a dominant board presence.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps is discarding to hand size and chose to discard Grave Endeavor, a 7-mana instant that reanimates a creature with +1/+1 counters and drains opponents. With a graveyard full of powerful creatures (Ashen Rider, Sun Titan, Karmic Guide, Meteor Golem, Sunblast Angel, etc.), Grave Endeavor would be an extremely powerful spell if cast. However, the player also has Unburial Rites in hand (which has flashback) and Sun Titan, both of which serve reanimation purposes. The key issue is that Grave Endeavor is an instant (castable at instant speed) and provides both reanimation AND life drain, making it arguably stronger than some alternatives to discard. That said, they're keeping both Sun Titan and Unburial Rites which together provide strong reanimation redundancy, and with only 6 lands in play, casting the 7-mana Grave Endeavor would take a while. Discarding a land like one of the Plains might have been better since they already have limited colored mana sources and Unburial Rites' flashback only needs white, while keeping the powerful instant for later. But with Rod of Absorption also in hand (which could exile instants/sorceries), the decision is debatable.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Grave Endeavor to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the two Plains instead, keeping Grave Endeavor as a powerful instant-speed reanimation spell that also drains opponents. With Unburial Rites already providing sorcery-speed reanimation (with flashback), Grave Endeavor adds instant-speed flexibility and the life drain component could matter in the endgame.

annotations.description: Casting Wall of Omens before playing a land means GPT5m Gramps goes from 8 cards in hand to 7 (cast) then 8 (draw from Wall), requiring a discard to 7. If they played a land first (going to 7 cards), then cast Wall of Omens (6 cards), then drew (7 cards), they'd avoid discarding entirely and have more mana available for whatever they draw.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Wall of Omens before playing a land for the turn
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (Plains or Island for untapped mana, or Arcane Sanctum), then cast Wall of Omens to avoid needing to discard and to have more mana available for any drawn card

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps is discarding to hand size and chose to discard Wall of Omens over a basic land. Wall of Omens is a 2-mana creature that draws a card on ETB, which has excellent synergy with Sun Titan (which can return it from the graveyard since it has MV 2), Karmic Guide, Unburial Rites, and other reanimation effects already in the graveyard. However, the player already has Sun Titan and Unburial Rites in hand as reanimation tools, and Wall of Omens in the graveyard is actually a fine Sun Titan target. The real issue is that they should discard one of the three basic lands (two Plains and an Island) instead, since they already have 6 lands on the battlefield and multiple lands in hand. A basic Plains would be the most expendable card - they already have Port Town and Nimbus Maze for white mana, and keeping Wall of Omens in hand allows casting it for value rather than relying on reanimation to get the draw.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Wall of Omens instead of a basic land
annotations.betterLine: Discard a Plains - GPT5m Gramps has two Plains and an Island in hand plus Arcane Sanctum, which is excessive land. Wall of Omens is a cheap cantrip creature that provides value whether cast from hand or reanimated by Sun Titan.

annotations.description: Attacking with all 4 creatures into Propaganda costs 8 mana (4×2), using all available mana and leaving nothing for interaction spells like Leadership Vacuum (2U) or Desperate Ravings (1R). The attack deals 20 to a 25-life opponent, which isn't lethal either way.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all creatures (Zetalpa, Pristine Skywise, Elsha, River Kelpie), paying 8 mana for Propaganda tax
annotations.betterLine: Attack with just Zetalpa and Pristine Skywise for 14 damage (4 mana Propaganda tax), keeping 4 mana open for interaction like Leadership Vacuum or Desperate Ravings. The extra 6 damage from Elsha and River Kelpie doesn't achieve lethal and leaves you completely tapped out.

annotations.description: Leadership Vacuum is a narrow instant that returns commanders to the command zone and draws a card. In this game state, Llama4 Valley has Pramikon on board (their own commander), and the only other living opponent is GPT5m Gramps who has no commander on the battlefield. However, Leadership Vacuum still cantrips (draws a card) for 3 mana, making it a cheap interaction piece. Meanwhile, Boros Guildgate and Mystic Monastery are tap-lands that could help fix mana, and the player already has 8 lands with decent color coverage. Discarding Boros Guildgate (a tap-land entering tapped that only produces R/W, colors already well-covered) would likely be better than discarding a cantripping interaction spell. Even if Leadership Vacuum's primary mode is less useful with no opposing commanders in play, the card replacement aspect gives it some floor value.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Leadership Vacuum
annotations.betterLine: Discard Boros Guildgate or Mystic Monastery, as these are redundant tap-lands when the player already has 8 lands, while Leadership Vacuum at least cantrips and could be relevant if GPT5m Gramps replays their commander.

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley passed priority during combat without using available instant-speed card draw. With 8 lands on the battlefield (enough mana available), they could have cast Think Twice (1U) or Desperate Ravings (1R) from hand to draw cards at end of combat or during this phase, using mana that would otherwise go unused. Think Twice also has flashback value later. Chemister's Insight (3U) was also castable. Drawing cards at instant speed during combat (or at end of opponent's turn) is pure upside when mana is available and going unused.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any instant-speed card draw spells despite having available mana and multiple options.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Think Twice or Desperate Ravings using available mana to draw cards, since this mana would likely go unused otherwise. These are best cast at end of turn or during combat to maximize information before committing.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps is in a 1v1 situation against Llama4 Valley (the other two players are eliminated at negative life). With only 6 lands in play (Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Port Town, Propaganda, Dungeon Map, Lightning Greaves - only 3 actual mana-producing lands plus artifacts), GPT5m Gramps desperately needs to reanimate threats. Rod of Absorption is a 3-mana artifact that's very slow and situational - it needs to be deployed, then accumulate exiled spells, then sacrificed. Meanwhile, discarding a land (Plains or Island) would be much better since the hand already has Unburial Rites (which can be cast from graveyard with flashback for 3W), Sun Titan (which can recur permanents), and Victimize. The reanimation plan is the clear path to victory. Discarding a Plains would actually help since Unburial Rites has white flashback cost and Sun Titan could recur it from the graveyard. However, Rod of Absorption is genuinely weak here in a late-game 1v1 with limited mana, so discarding it isn't terrible. The real issue is that discarding one of the extra Plains copies would be strictly better - they have two Plains in hand plus Arcane Sanctum, and the Plains are less useful than Rod of Absorption which at least has some theoretical upside.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Rod of Absorption
annotations.betterLine: Discard a Plains instead. With two Plains, an Island, and Arcane Sanctum in hand, one Plains is redundant. Rod of Absorption, while slow, is at least a unique effect that could provide value if the game goes long, whereas an extra basic land when you already have multiple lands to play is less valuable.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps cast Doomed Necromancer (a 3-mana creature that needs to survive a turn cycle to activate) before playing a land. They have Plains, Island, and Arcane Sanctum in hand but only 6 lands on the battlefield (Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Propaganda uses no land slot, Port Town, Dungeon Map, Lightning Greaves - actually only Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Port Town are lands plus some artifacts). More critically, casting Doomed Necromancer with only 3 mana available (if that) means they can't also play a land and advance their mana development. They should play a land first before casting spells. Additionally, with Sun Titan and Unburial Rites in hand alongside powerful reanimation targets in the graveyard (Ashen Rider, Karmic Guide, Meteor Golem, Sunblast Angel), the better play would be to play a land (Arcane Sanctum or Plains) to build toward casting Unburial Rites (4B) or Sun Titan (4WW) next turn. Doomed Necromancer requires surviving a full turn cycle AND having B mana available, making it slow and vulnerable compared to just casting Unburial Rites when they have enough mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Doomed Necromancer before playing a land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (Arcane Sanctum for color fixing, or Plains), then cast Doomed Necromancer if still desired. Prioritizing land drops to reach Unburial Rites or Sun Titan mana sooner would be more impactful.

annotations.description: Discarding Island instead of a duplicate Plains loses blue mana access. With Nimbus Maze on the battlefield (which produces U only if you control a Plains, and W only if you control an Island), keeping the Island is valuable since they already have two Plains and Arcane Sanctum for white mana. Playing an Island would let Nimbus Maze tap for U, providing better color diversity.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Island
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the two Plains instead, keeping the Island for blue mana diversity and to enable Nimbus Maze to produce U.

annotations.description: Thalia's Geistcaller has strong synergy with Llama4 Valley's graveyard-heavy strategy (many flashback spells in graveyard like Sevinne's Reclamation, Ignite the Future, Divine Reckoning, etc.), creating spirit tokens and providing lifelink. Boros Guildgate is a tapped land providing R/W colors already available from existing lands.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Thalia's Geistcaller
annotations.betterLine: Discard Boros Guildgate, which enters tapped and provides colors already covered by existing lands. Thalia's Geistcaller would generate significant value with the many flashback spells available in the graveyard.

annotations.description: Reassembling Skeleton is a recursive creature that can return itself from the graveyard to the battlefield for {1}{B}, making it arguably better in the graveyard than in hand. However, GPT5m Gramps has powerful reanimation spells (Unburial Rites, Victimize, Sun Titan) and reanimation targets (Ashen Rider, Karmic Guide, Meteor Golem, Sunblast Angel) in the graveyard. Discarding Reassembling Skeleton is reasonable since it functions from the graveyard, but discarding a Plains instead could be considered since they already have lands on the battlefield and Plains in the graveyard. The Skeleton does serve as a sacrifice outlet for Victimize, which is relevant. On the other hand, keeping both Plains ensures land drops for future turns to cast expensive spells like Sun Titan (6 mana) and Unburial Rites (5 mana). With only 6 lands in play, land drops are still important. Discarding the Skeleton is defensible since it works from the graveyard, but a Plains could have been discarded instead since they have multiple Plains already.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Reassembling Skeleton
annotations.betterLine: Discarding a Plains instead, since GPT5m already has Plains on board and in graveyard, while keeping Reassembling Skeleton in hand preserves the option to cast it as a creature for Victimize sacrifice fodder without spending the {1}{B} recursion cost. Though the Skeleton does function from graveyard, having it in hand gives more flexibility.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps is discarding down to hand size and chose to discard Necrotic Sliver. While Necrotic Sliver isn't the strongest card in hand, it's a creature that could be reanimated from the graveyard (which is fine since they have reanimation spells). However, the real question is whether discarding a Plains or Arcane Sanctum would have been better. They already have very few lands on the battlefield (only 4 mana-producing lands: Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Port Town, plus Dungeon Map for colorless) and desperately need to play lands to cast their expensive spells like Sun Titan (6 mana) and Unburial Rites (5 mana). Keeping both Plains and Arcane Sanctum seems correct for land drops. Necrotic Sliver is a reasonable discard since it can be reanimated later and is less impactful than the reanimation package (Victimize, Unburial Rites, Doomed Necromancer, Sun Titan). The discard is defensible but one could argue that Doomed Necromancer might be better to discard since it also goes to the graveyard where it can be reanimated, and Necrotic Sliver's sacrifice-to-destroy ability is quite strong in this board state where Llama4 Valley has threats like Zetalpa and Pramikon.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Necrotic Sliver
annotations.betterLine: Discard is reasonable since Necrotic Sliver can be reanimated later, but discarding a Plains instead could also be justified since they already have Plains in graveyard for potential recursion and Necrotic Sliver's destroy ability is very relevant against Llama4 Valley's board.

annotations.description: Desperate Ravings has flashback {2}{U}, meaning it can be cast from the graveyard for value later (draw 2, discard 1 at random). With Llama4 Valley running a graveyard-synergy deck (River Kelpie triggers on graveyard casts, Sevinne's Reclamation, etc.), flashback cards in the graveyard are valuable resources. Meanwhile, Azorius Locket is a 3-mana rock that's mediocre at this stage when they already have 7+ lands, and Azorius Chancery is a tapland that bounces a land. Either of those would be less impactful discards than a flashback spell.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Desperate Ravings, a card with flashback that synergizes with their graveyard strategy.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Azorius Locket or Azorius Chancery instead, as they provide less future value than a flashback spell in a deck that benefits from casting spells from the graveyard.

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley has flashback spells available and mana open during combat (likely end of turn timing). Think Twice (flashback {2}{U}) and Desperate Ravings (flashback {2}{U}) could be cast from the graveyard to draw cards, and Oona's Grace could be cast with retrace by discarding a land. With 9 lands on the battlefield (including Temple of the False God), there's likely enough mana to cast at least one of these card-draw spells. Passing priority without using available mana sinks wastes potential card advantage, especially since this appears to be an end-of-turn window where unused mana would go to waste.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells, leaving mana unused.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Think Twice from graveyard for its flashback cost ({2}{U}) or Desperate Ravings from graveyard for its flashback cost ({2}{U}) to draw cards with otherwise unused mana.

annotations.description: Mystic Retrieval returns a target instant or sorcery from graveyard to hand. Ignite the Future costs 3R and exiles top 3 cards to play until end of next turn, but with only 8 lands (some tapped) and needing to recast it, the value is uncertain. Meanwhile, Sevinne's Reclamation (2W, flashback 4W) could return a permanent with MV 3 or less from graveyard to battlefield - potentially getting back Burning Vengeance, Burnished Hart, Command Tower, or other valuable permanents. Deep Analysis (flashback 1U, pay 3 life) could also be retrieved for efficient card draw. Think Twice is cheap flashback draw. The choice of Ignite the Future is defensible as a high-ceiling play, but given the current board state with only Pramikon as a real permanent and needing to rebuild, Sevinne's Reclamation would likely provide more consistent value by recurring key permanents like Burning Vengeance or Dockside Extortionist directly to the battlefield.
annotations.actionTaken: Retrieved Ignite the Future with Mystic Retrieval
annotations.betterLine: Retrieve Sevinne's Reclamation to recur key low-MV permanents like Burning Vengeance, Dockside Extortionist, or Command Tower from the graveyard to the battlefield, providing more reliable board development

However, Devil's Play is a flexible win condition. Azorius Chancery is a reasonable discard given the tempo loss of bouncing a land, so this is debatable rather than clearly wrong.

annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any instant-speed spells.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Think Twice from graveyard for its flashback cost ({2}{U}) or Desperate Ravings from graveyard ({2}{U}) to draw cards at instant speed while the mana would otherwise go unused.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Think Twice from graveyard (flashback {2}{U}) or Desperate Ravings from graveyard (flashback {2}{U}) to draw cards at instant speed, using otherwise wasted mana.

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley is in a 1v1 situation against GPT5m Gramps (25hp) with both Kimi25 Libby and MiMo Timmy eliminated. Valley has 39 life and only Pramikon on board but has 8 lands (7 untapped after Swiftwater Cliffs is tapped). They have flashback spells available in graveyard and cards like Think Twice, Desperate Ravings, and Chemister's Insight that could be cast from graveyard to dig for action. With Temple of the False God providing 2 mana, they have access to significant mana. Casting Think Twice from graveyard (flashback {2}{U}) or Desperate Ravings from graveyard (flashback {2}{U}) during their own main phase would help find threats or answers. More importantly, they should be deploying threats - they could cast Backdraft Hellkite (3RR) which would be excellent as it gives all instants/sorceries in graveyard flashback when it attacks. They have the mana for it with Mountain + Temple of the False God + Islands. Passing without doing anything in main phase wastes development time.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting anything during precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Backdraft Hellkite for {3}{R}{R} using Mountain, Temple of the False God, and Islands (via Pramikon's color identity allowing the mana). Alternatively, at minimum cast Think Twice or Desperate Ravings from graveyard to draw cards and develop board position against the remaining opponent.

annotations.description: Discarded Darkwater Catacombs (a UB-producing land) when mana-starved with only 6 lands on board. The hand contains two Plains and an Arcane Sanctum which already covers white mana. Darkwater Catacombs would have provided access to black and blue mana needed for key reanimation spells like Unburial Rites, Victimize, and Doomed Necromancer.
